Nice — you want concrete options (libs + frameworks) **and runnable code patterns** you can use now to generate videos. I’ll give: - a quick taxonomy (when to use what), - the current best-in-class AI models / services (what people use today), - recommended libraries & frameworks (Python & JS), - two compact, copy-pasteable examples: 1. Python: generate many image frames (Diffusion) → stitch into a video with MoviePy, and 2. JS: programmatic/synthetic video with Remotion (React-based). - short pros/cons, and pointers for safety / licensing. I looked up the modern tools and models so you get up-to-date options (sources shown inline). --- # 1) Quick taxonomy — pick by goal - **Programmatic / generative animation (code-driven):** use Remotion, Three.js, p5.js, Manim — good for charts, generative art, UI-driven video. citeturn0search3turn0search7 - **Frame-by-frame neural generation (diffusion/GAN → video):** create many image frames with a text-to-image model (or an image-to-image/video model) then stitch to video. Use Hugging Face Diffusers, StabilityAI Stable Video Diffusion (SVD), or community scripts. citeturn0search13turn0search1turn0search5 - **End-to-end text-to-video APIs / hosted products:** Runway Gen-2, OpenAI Sora, Adobe Firefly Video, Meta MovieGen — these give direct T2V (usually short clips, closed / limited access). citeturn0search0turn0news44turn0news49turn0news50 --- # 2) Recommended libs & frameworks (practical list) **Python (good for research / prototyping + assembly)** - `diffusers` (Hugging Face) — for Stable Diffusion style generation. (use to create frames). citeturn0search12 - `stabilityai` / Stable Video Diffusion (SVD) repos / community notebooks — image→video models. citeturn0search1turn0search13 - `moviepy` — stitch frames, add audio, export MP4. citeturn0search6 - `opencv-python` (cv2) — frame manipulation, optical flow, filters. citeturn0search2 - `imageio` / `PyAV` — alternative readers/writers to FFmpeg. citeturn0search2turn0search10 **JavaScript / Node / Web (production / interactive / websites)** - `Remotion` (React-based video-by-code) — great for procedurally generated, data-driven videos and server-side rendering. citeturn0search3 - `Three.js` + `@remotion/three` — 3D scenes for Remotion. citeturn0search7 - `p5.js` — quick generative visuals (2D). - `ffmpeg` (CLI) — always useful for final encoding; use wrappers like `fluent-ffmpeg` for Node. **Hosted / API-first text-to-video (if you want the easiest path)** - Runway (Gen-2), OpenAI (Sora), Stability AI (SVD / services), Adobe Firefly Video, Meta MovieGen. These are easiest but may be gated or have quota/cost. citeturn0search0turn0news44turn0search1turn0news49turn0news50 --- # 3) Example A — Python pipeline: generate frames (Diffusion) → stitch to video This is a practical pattern used widely: use a text-to-image model to make N frames (varying prompt/seed or a conditioning frame) then combine frames to MP4 with MoviePy. Install: ```bash pip install diffusers transformers torch accelerate safetensors moviepy # plus any GPU driver / CUDA libs if you have a GPU ``` Minimal example (generate frames with Hugging Face `diffusers` stable-diffusion image model, then assemble): ```python # generate_and_stitch.py from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline import torch from moviepy.editor import ImageSequenceClip prompt = "A cinematic cinematic sunset over futuristic city, wide angle" num_frames = 30 width, height = 512, 512 fps = 15 out_video = "out.mp4" # Load pipeline (use your HF token if required) pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained( "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5", torch_dtype=torch.float16 ) pipe = pipe.to("cuda") frames = [] for i in range(num_frames): # You can vary seed, prompt or add small prompt modifications to animate seed = 42 + i generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed) img = pipe(prompt, height=height, width=width, num_inference_steps=20, generator=generator).images[0] # save to temp or keep in memory frames.append(img) # MoviePy: convert PIL images to video # frames is list of PIL images — convert to numpy arrays if needed clip = ImageSequenceClip([frame for frame in frames], fps=fps) clip.write_videofile(out_video, codec="libx264") ``` Notes & tips: - This produces a choppy, frame-by-frame video unless you ensure continuity: interpolate between latents or use an image-to-image motion prior (Stable Video Diffusion, SVD) for smoother motion. Community projects (SVD & “latent interpolation” scripts) are common. citeturn0search1turn0search5 - If you need smoother temporal coherence, look into **Stable Video Diffusion / SVD** or latent interpolation techniques (community repos). citeturn0search1turn0search5 --- # 4) Example B — JS: programmatic video with Remotion (React) Remotion lets you compose frames in React (SVG / Canvas / Three.js), then render MP4 server-side. Install & quick start: ```bash npx create-video@latest my-video cd my-video npm run start # dev server npm run build # render ``` Simple Remotion component: ```jsx // src/Video.jsx import {Composition} from 'remotion'; import { MyVideo } from './MyVideo'; export const RemotionRoot = () => { return ( <> ); }; // src/MyVideo.jsx import {Sequence, staticFile} from 'remotion'; export const MyVideo = () => { return (
Hello—Remotion video by code!
); }; ``` Why Remotion: - Works with React, JSX, and existing web tooling; perfect for templated, data-driven videos (e.g., 1000 personalized clips). citeturn0search3 --- # 5) Short pros/cons & recommended stacks **If you want photoreal short clips from text (no coding of frames):** - Use hosted services (Runway Gen-2, OpenAI Sora, Adobe, Meta demos). Fastest, best continuity, but costs & usage constraints. citeturn0search0turn0news44turn0news49 **If you want control / run locally / research:** - Use `diffusers` + frame stitching (MoviePy/FFmpeg). Adds flexibility, but you must manage temporal coherence yourself. Use SVD or community colabs to improve motion. citeturn0search13turn0search9 **If you want programmatic motion/graphics (charts, animations):** - Use Remotion (React) or Manim (Python) — deterministic, production-ready. citeturn0search3 --- # 6) Safety, costs and licensing (short) - Hosted T2V often has content safety filters and usage limits (and may be unavailable in some regions). Check each provider’s license before using generated content commercially. Example: OpenAI Sora rollout had region limits and content restrictions. citeturn0news44 - Many pre-trained ML models have specific license/usage terms (Stability AI models often require reviewing Stability’s license for commercial use). citeturn0search13 --- # 7) Where to start (practical path I recommend) 1. If you want fast results: try **Runway Gen-2** or **OpenAI Sora** (hosted) to see what T2V can do. citeturn0search0turn0news44 2. If you want to build and learn: do the Python flow — `diffusers` (image) → MoviePy (stitch). Then graduate to Stable Video Diffusion / SVD repos for better motion. citeturn0search1turn0search5 3. If you need scale/personalization: build templates in **Remotion** and/or integrate API-generated frames as assets. --- If you want, tell me which of the three paths above you want to follow (a) **hosted T2V quick test**, (b) **local diffusion frames → stitch** (I’ll give a more robust script with latent interpolation), or (c) **programmatic video with Remotion** — and I’ll drop a full, runnable starter repo for that path right now (code + requirements + short README). No fluff — just the exact files you need. Which one?
